can_do_statement: Can report requests and commands with 'ask' or 'tell' + direct object and 'to-'infinitive.

ontology.mental_model: Reported directives mapping a speaker's instruction onto an object via to-infinitive.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Reporting someone else's command or request.

positives: She asked me to come back early.
They told the students to stay in the car.
negatives: I want to ask a question.
He told a story to his friends.

guideword: FORM: DIRECT SPEECH, REPORTING CLAUSE, END POSITION
can_do_statement: Can report speech and thought directly using the reporting verb after the reporting clause.

ontology.mental_model: Direct quotation structured with the reporting clause at the end.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Putting the quoted speech first, then saying who said it.

positives: "I am leaving," she said.
"What is going on?" he asked.
negatives: She said, "I am leaving."
He asked what was going on.

guideword: FORM: DIRECT SPEECH, REPORTING CLAUSE, INITIAL POSITION
can_do_statement: Can report speech and thought directly, using the reporting verb before the reporting clause.

ontology.mental_model: Direct quotation structured with the reporting clause at the beginning.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Saying who spoke before giving their exact words.

positives: She said: "I am going home."
He asked, "Are you coming?"
negatives: "I am going home," she said.
He told me that he was tired.

can_do_statement: Can report thought using 'wonder' + 'wh-'word + clause, with a tense shift where relevant.

ontology.mental_model: Expressing an internal question or uncertainty using 'wonder' followed by a wh-clause.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'wonder' to talk about thoughts and questions.

positives: I wondered what she had written.
He was wondering who the mysterious guest was.
negatives: I wonder if it will rain tomorrow.
It's a wonder how they survived.

can_do_statement: Can modify the reporting verb with an adverb.

ontology.mental_model: Modifying a reporting verb with an adverb to express the manner of speech.

positives: "I won't do it," she said forcefully.
He asked curiously about the details.
negatives: She quickly finished the work.
I suddenly thought of an idea.

guideword: FORM: DIRECT SPEECH, REPORTING CLAUSE, MID POSITION
can_do_statement: Can report speech and thought directly using the reporting verb in the mid position of the reported clause.

ontology.mental_model: Interrupting a direct quote with the reporting clause in the middle.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Putting the "he said" part in the middle of a quote.

positives: "No problem", I thought, "there is only one person".
"Forgive me", he said, "I will never leave."
negatives: "No problem, there is only one person," I thought.
He said, "Forgive me, I will never leave."

guideword: FORM: DIRECT SPEECH, REPORTING CLAUSE, INVERTED SUBJECT
can_do_statement: Can report speech directly inverting the subject and verb in the reporting clause where the subject is a proper noun or noun phrase.

ontology.mental_model: Reporting speech using verb-subject order when the subject is a noun phrase.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using "said John" instead of "John said" after a quote.

positives: "I was astonished", said John.
"Who are you?" asked Peter.
negatives: "I was astonished," John said.
John said he was astonished.

can_do_statement: Can use the past continuous of the reporting verb to report mental processes, with a finite or non-finite 'wh-'clause in the reported clause.

ontology.mental_model: Reporting a continuous past mental state or process.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using past continuous (was wondering, was thinking) to report thoughts.

positives: I was wondering why I failed.
While he was thinking how to reply, she left.
negatives: I wondered why I failed.
He was walking down the street.

can_do_statement: Can use the present simple form of the reporting verb to report information from a written source and a present tense verb in the reported clause.

ontology.mental_model: Reporting information from written sources as an enduring fact using present simple.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'says' or 'tells' to talk about what's written in a book, sign, or article.

positives: The guidebook says that we can get there by train.
Your advertisement tells us about the hotel.
negatives: He says he is coming.
The book was very interesting.

guideword: FORM: REPORTED REQUESTS AND COMMANDS, NEGATIVE
can_do_statement: Can report requests and commands with 'ask' or 'tell' + direct object + 'not' + 'to-'infinitive.

ontology.mental_model: Reporting a negative directive using not + to-infinitive.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Reporting negative commands like 'told him not to do it'.

positives: She told me not to be scared.
I asked Pat not to tell anyone.
negatives: She told me to be careful.
I asked him not for money, but for advice.

can_do_statement: Can report speech about events in the past with backshifts for tenses and words relating to time.

ontology.mental_model: Backshifting tenses and temporal adverbs when reporting past events.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using past perfect in reported speech for events further in the past.

positives: She had told me the previous day that it was important.
I had told my friends the day before that I expected an A.
negatives: She told me yesterday that it was important.
I had told my friends that I liked the movie.

can_do_statement: Can use linking verb 'be' with complements.

ontology.mental_model: Linking an entity to a state or attribute using the copula.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'be' to describe something or someone.

positives: Because today is my birthday.
Martin is from Poland.
negatives: He is running fast.
They were playing outside.

can_do_statement: Can use a wide range of linking verbs with complements.

ontology.mental_model: Using a wide range of linking verbs (seem, appear, remain, taste, sound) with adjectival or nominal complements.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using more advanced linking verbs to describe states.

positives: It all seems very confusing.
The whole house appeared very unfamiliar.
negatives: He tasted the soup.
She appeared in the doorway.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of linking verbs with complements.

ontology.mental_model: Using an increasing range of linking verbs (look, become, get, feel) with adjectival complements.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using linking verbs to talk about changes or feelings.

positives: It looks good on you.
Make sure they won't get dirty.
negatives: He looked at the picture.
I got a new car.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of verbs, typically reporting, with a 'that'-clause as the direct object.

ontology.mental_model: Reporting thoughts or statements using a reporting verb followed by an explicit 'that' clause.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'that' to introduce a reported statement.

positives: I hope that you'll come.
My mother said that she can help us.
negatives: I hope you'll come.
He pointed at the book that was on the table.
